name: ★ STACK · the R19 stand, resumed and left alone (watch)

name: PROBE · push test — 3 N shoves on the R19 stand every 60 s (watch)

hint: R19 catches 2 N 35/36 and 3 N 13/36. Change the force to bracket a brain's envelope; Report reads it. Point 'a saved brain' at the brain under test.

hint: The guard: run it before touching code, keep the JSONL, run it again after, cmp.

name: PROBE · scaffold — shove Pollen's standing policy (5 N every 4 s, watch)
hint: The RL reference: staggers and catches 5 N, knocked over at 10 N and stands back up. The envelope the brain is measured against.

name: PROBE · recovery harness — the stub brain that falls over (watch)
hint: A brain that fails, the scaffold that picks it up, and the hand-off between them. Tests the harness, not the substrate.

name: ★ STACK · find from scratch (R19, 2 h, headless, saves the brain) — every seed stands in 15 min
hint: R19: a settle before every identification pulse window. All six seeds consolidate inside 15 min, 2-3 rescues in 2 h, tilt 0.35°, |u| 0.18; the brain catches 2 N shoves. Tick 'battery' for seeds 1-6.

name: ★ STACK · watch the catch — 2 N shoves on the R19 stand every 20 s (watch)
hint: Resume duck_r19_s2 under R19 and shove it: the ball stays green, tilt peaks ~2.7° and the body is back inside 0.6 s. Raise to 3 N to see where it still goes over (fore-aft first).

name: ★ STACK · the step — 3 N shoves on the R19 stand with the walker's hand-off (watch)
hint: Phase 0/1a of the intent boundary: when the brain's own attitude-prior error passes 0.06 and is rising, the joints go to the walker (yellow ball), which staggers through it, then back to the brain. Measured across six brains: 3 N 36/36 upright (13/36 without), 5 N 30/36 (6/36 without), never at 1 N, two false hand-offs in 36 at 2 N.

name: ★ STACK · a walk on request — 4 s forward at 0.3 m/s, then back to the reflex (watch)
hint: Phase 1b of the intent boundary: at 10 s the joints go to Pollen's walking policy with a forward command (blue ball), it walks ~0.5 m, settles, and hands back to the brain, which is quiet again within seconds. Change vx/vy/vyaw to steer; the policy stands still below ~0.25 m/s.

name: R20 · level-2 identification — twist babble at the walker (700 s, headless, saves the brain)
hint: Phase 1e of the intent boundary: the same module one level up. Motors = the three twist commands to Pollen's walker, senses = the body's own velocity from contact odometry and the gyro. Held 1.5 s twist pulses, one axis at a time. The host prints the identified A at the end: a positive, dominant diagonal is the gate (passed: 0.0083 / 0.0040 / 0.0090).

name: R21 · level-2 prior: walk straight — prior-only (HK on spins); 0.21 m/s, straightness 0.90 (headless, 1500 s)
hint: The first level-2 control (design doc §16.5): a state prior on the sensed forward velocity (slot 0, target 0.75 of the 0.4 m/s range = 0.3 m/s) and on the yaw rate (slot 6, target 0), with the controller learning (ctrl_lr 0.1) through the A that R20 identified. Babble 600 s, then the prior drives. Judged on forward speed and heading drift over the control phase against the walker under a constant forward command, which drifts 5-8 deg/s by itself.

name: R22 · level-2 heading regulation — shoves during the walk, the brain turns back (headless, 1500 s)
hint: The (d) test at the intent boundary (§16.6): after 600 s of babble the brain walks at the walker's top speed holding its heading; 2 N shoves every 40 s turn it 17-20°, and it is back within 3-4° twenty seconds later, 20/20, no rescues. The open-loop walker (--l2-twist 0.4 0 0) ends 109° off. Switch to watch to see it; the ball is blue while the walker drives.

name: R23 · level-2 avoidance in the arena — zero wall contacts, but an orbit (headless, 1500 s)
hint: Phase 2a: the ToF proximities enter the level-2 sense and a prior of zero on them plus the walk-forward prior gives 0 wall contacts in 25 min (open loop: 46/min; walk-straight: 194/min, pinned to a wall). But it orbits: 167 m inside nine 0.25 m cells. Avoidance is a constraint, not a drive — R24 adds the novelty drive. Watch it with scene_arena.xml; the beams draw from the head.

name: R24 · level-2 map + surprise prior in the arena — NULL: the map learns, the prior has no gradient (headless, 1500 s)
hint: Phase 2b first probe (§17.3): the map EPM over place reaches 34 nodes for 33 cells under a touring walker and its surprise falls as the arena becomes familiar; but the identified A row for surprise is zero, so a prior on it moves nothing and the R23 orbit stays. Kept as the record.

name: R25 · level-2 wander by boredom + heading + avoidance — REGRESSION: rides the walls (headless, 1500 s)
hint: Phase 2b second probe (§17.4): with the heading prior back, the body rides the walls at ~290 contacts/min because the heading row outweighs the barely identified proximity rows; 32 boredom-driven heading changes did not change coverage. The arbitration question, measured. Run with --wander-bored 8 --wander-turn 90 for the rule.

name: R26 · level-2 keeps learning after the babble (babble_owns_a 0) — the regression gone at n=6
hint: WATCH (seed 2; 25 min in real time, the babble ends at 600 s): after the babble the body settles into a small loop — 1.3 wall contacts/min, 25 cells. Seed 5 is the other attractor: a tour of 60 cells at 52 contacts/min. n=6: 26 ± 35/min against R25's 295. Exactly the harness run (arena, reset noise 0.05).

name: R26 · moved wall (d): the +x wall shifts at 1100 s — R26 keeps its habits, contacts fall, the map does not grow
hint: WATCH (seed 2; 30 min): the +x wall moves at 1100 s. R26 keeps its loop — 0.9 contacts/min over the run, 28 cells, and the map does not grow (n=6 after the move: contacts 47 → 29/min, nodes 31 → 28). Robust, but no re-exploration: the (d) bar's re-inference half is NULL here.

name: R27 · level-2 where-to-go: the play loop's novelty climb over the map sets the heading (§17.3 fork a)
hint: WATCH (seed 6): the play loop's novelty bearing sets the heading — the body tours 54 cells at 1.6 contacts/min and turns away from walls it knows. Seed 1 never leaves an orbit (12 cells, 8 map nodes: too few places for a route). n=6: 9 ± 9/min, 42 cells.

name: R27 · moved wall (d): the +x wall shifts at 1100 s — play drives at the wall it 'knows' is open (253/min after the move)
hint: WATCH (seed 6): the seed that toured cleanly in the steady arena drives at the moved wall — the novel region is where the wall now stands: 222 contacts/min over the run (n=6 after the move: 253 ± 143, map +22 nodes). A learned direction beats the proximity priors when the two conflict.

name: R28 · level-2 avoid vs novelty ARBITRATED — the Cell recipe on the duck (need × competence over loops with bearings)
hint: WATCH (seed 5): near a wall the avoidance loop wins and puts its away-bearing on the heading reference — and the body barely turns: 43 contacts/min here, 71 ± 80 at n=6, seed 3 rides the wall at 224. The bearing form, kept for the record; R29 is the same seed in the release form.

name: R28 · moved wall (d): the +x wall shifts at 1100 s — the bearing form stops the burst hardest, and the re-exploration with it
hint: WATCH (seed 5): avoidance's bearing wins near the moved wall and stops the burst hardest (n=6 after the move: 114/min) and the re-exploration with it (nodes 42 → 33). This seed: 31 contacts/min over the run but a short path (74 m) — it moves little after the shift.

name: R29 · level-2 arbitration, the release form — avoidance yields the heading to the reflex
hint: WATCH (seed 5): near a wall the avoidance loop wins and RELEASES the heading so the proximity reflex acts — 17 contacts/min here against R28's 43 on the same seed (n=6: 44 ± 62), still a tour (56 cells). In a known room play alone (R27) is the better avoider.

name: R29 · moved wall (d): the +x wall shifts at 1100 s — the release form cuts R27's burst by 40 % and keeps half its re-exploration
hint: WATCH (seed 5): after the wall moves the release form cuts R27's burst by 40 % (n=6 after the move: 149 vs 253/min) and keeps half its re-exploration (nodes +10 vs +22). This seed: 107 contacts/min over the run, 58 cells.

name: R30 · the PLAYROOM: R27's play loop in the 4 m room (A1, the room is the lever)
hint: WATCH (seed 6): the same play loop as R27 in the 4 m playroom (seed-1 room, walls 1 m, an angled sun). THE FIRST 600 s ARE THE BABBLE — the duck identifies its twist model in place; the tour starts at 600 s, so this preset fast-forwards to there (the run is tick-for-tick the harness run). Furniture counts as wall contact; ball/block contact is the obj flag; the clock hand turns once per 20 s. n=6: 7.1 ± 6.0 walls/min, 151 ± 34 cells of 256, 100 ± 20 map nodes, 0.07 objs/min — nothing seeks the movables yet.

name: R30 · moved ball (d): obj_ball0 jumps across the room at 1100 s — does the map re-explore where it went?
hint: WATCH (seed 6): fast-forwards through the 600 s babble; at 1100 s the red ball is relocated to (-1.2, 0.8), across the room from where the map knows it. The (d) test for the playroom: whether the novelty climb goes to the new place.

name: R31 · H1 the HEAD LOOP: identification babble on the four head commands, the walker standing (watch the head)
hint: WATCH (seed 2): the head babbles for 600 s in 0.5 s holds at 0.3 of its trained ranges while the walker stands; the identified rows print at the end (stderr). n=5: every position diagonal positive, the pitches opposite-signed on head-gravity x, roll on y, 0 rescues. No fast-forward: the babble IS the thing to watch.

name: R33 · H2 the HEAD LOOP, slow prior: level on two motors, model frozen, state_prior_lr 0.02 (less rail-chasing; compare with R32 and R30)
hint: WATCH (seed 6) against R32 and R30: the head still level fore-aft, the roll and pitch commands bang their rails less. The picture is steadier than R32 and still not as steady as the walker's own head.

name: ★ HEAD · Track A at the joints: the head brain owns the head, level and steadier than the walker's own (R34)
hint: PROMOTED (operator's eye, 2026-09-11): a significant improvement in stability over R30; the wobble tolerable through the head camera, the walk more birdlike. Seed 6, fast-forward through the babble: the head is ours at the joints — level, yaw wobble 91 → 58 deg/s, picture 12.3 → 9.9. Compare with R30 (the walker's head) and R33 (the same loop through robot.head).

name: R39 · W1 walk-stop-STAND: scheduled stops after the babble; the R19 joint brain takes the legs when still (★ HEAD stack)
hint: The walk-stop-look line's first lever (playroom plan §12.7 W1): every 60 s from 600 s the twist is zeroed for 20 s; once still, the legs (and head) are handed to the R19 stander (checkpoint duck_r19_s2), which stands and catches; the walker takes them back past 6.5 deg of lean or at the stop's end. Judged on survival at the hand-back, handoffs, rescues, and the W0 histogram; the control is the same stops held by the walker (--stop-brain walker). The lever lives in the host args, the graph is R34's.

name: R40 · W2 stop-and-LOOK: at each stop the head brain keeps the head and its yaw scans 0, +0.6, 0, -0.6 rad (1 s holds) while the R19 stander holds the legs
hint: WATCH (seed 6, fast-forward through the 600 s babble): every 60 s the duck stops for 20 s — the walker settles, the R19 stander takes the legs (green), the head brain keeps the head level and its yaw steps 0, +0.6, 0, −0.6 rad, 1 s each; then the walk resumes. n=6: 90/90 stands held, 0 rescues at stops, 13 ± 5 walls/min (R39 18 ± 24) with the head brain frozen through the stop (design doc §17.19).

name: R41 · W3 a place is a STOP: the map learns only while standing, a view is pose + gaze, the look is driven by the map's own novelty (a quiet round ends the stop)
hint: WATCH (seed 6, fast-forward through the 600 s babble): every 80 s the duck stops; the R19 stander takes the legs (green), the head brain keeps the head level and looks 0, +0.6, −0.6 rad, holding a bearing while the map has not baked that view; a round with nothing new ends the stop (up to 60 s). The map learns only at stops. n=6: stops shorten as the map bakes (37 → 35 s), 5.4 walls/min capped form, 11/11 stands held (design doc §17.20).

name: R41 · moved chair (d): furn_chair0 jumps to the room's centre at 1100 s — the stops there lengthen and the duck comes to look
hint: WATCH (seed 6): as R41, and at 1100 s the chair is relocated to (0.3, 0.3). n=6: stops within 1.2 m of it go 38.6 → 45.7 s and the duck stops there 15 times where the unmoved run stops 3 (§17.20 addendum). The (d) test for a place that is a stop.

name: R42 · W3b the gaze BABBLES: at a stop the head takes random yaw and small pitch steps, dwelling where the map has not baked the view; the stop ends when nothing new has been seen for a while
hint: The operator (2026-09-12): the three-bearing round is a schedule; let the head babble while standing and reduce the scene's error. Random gaze steps (sd yaw 0.35, pitch 0.08 rad) each held 0.5 s and, while the view's winner is unbaked, up to 6 s; six known gazes in a row end the stop. The map learns only at stops; the head brain keeps the head, frozen. n=6: 65/66 stands held, stops 31 s, 92 % end on a quiet round, 41 views inserted / 21 baked per run, no baked view ever pruned; full pitch (sd 0.2) tips the stand — register O36.

name: R43 · W3c the place is LEARNED: bake at 20 visits and dwell on learning progress — a view that surprised the map is held until its error halves; the map keeps every view it bakes
hint: O37, the operator's watch item (2026-09-12): with baking at 50 visits half the views a stop inserts died unbaked; at 20 the map keeps them but the bake flag stops meaning novel. The dwell now holds a view that surprised the map on arrival (quant_error above the channel's expected error) while its error is still above half its arrival value — the map's own learning progress. n=6: 43 nodes with 42 baked at the end (the fullest map), 66/66 stands, 10 ± 6 walls/min, stops 46 s with the duck standing 53 % of the run — the stop's ending rule is now the design knob (design doc §17.23).

name: R44 · W3d the ORIENTING REFLEX: something moves while the duck looks — the stop ends, it turns to the gaze's bearing and walks there; a chair is carried past at every stop
hint: Agreed 2026-09-12: a change during a still gaze should trigger interest in that direction. While the gaze is still, a jump of the view's error 4 spreads above the hold's own mean, confirmed on two samples that touch two different ToF columns (the sensor flickers at edges; a mover crosses columns), ends the stop; the body pivots to the gaze bearing and walks with a P on the dead-reckoned yaw until it has covered ~1 m, then stops to look. n=6: a person-sized mover (the chair) is caught 57 % of crossings, a rolling ball 42 %, one unprompted orientation per ~15 min, every orientation arrives, 0.36 m from where the ball was; the stand untouched (design doc §17.24).

name: R48 · W5(b) the command COMPUTED from the model: the prior's error solved through the identified A each tick — the duck stops hitting things (walls 14.8 → 1.8/min) while covering the same room
hint: WATCH (seed 6, fast-forward through the 600 s babble): same walk-stop-look duck as R43, with one change in the twist brain — the command that closes the prior's errors is SOLVED through the model each tick instead of being learned into C. n=6: wall contact 14.8 → 1.8/min on every seed and 4.58 → 0.65 episodes per metre, with cells (69.7 → 73.8) and span (10.17 → 10.23) tied, so it is not R23's never-approach-anything orbit — seed 3 goes from 34.1 walls/min on 56 cells to ZERO on 89. What to watch for: the heading is unchanged (it still wanders — §17.27 NULL), and the stops now run the full 60 s on every seed instead of ending early (O37's ending rule), so it stands more and walks less. PARTIAL, not promoted (design doc §17.27).

name: R46 · the CLOUD at every stop: the stop's ToF returns accumulate into a voxel cloud (ogma::CloudMap) filed under the map's place; the gaze BABBLES, holding each angle
hint: WATCH (seed 3, fast-forward through the 600 s babble; P draws the filed clouds, N solos a place): the R43 walk-stop-look duck with CloudMap listening. The control for R52: at each stop the head steps to a random angle within +-0.7 rad and HOLDS it 1-6 s -- its joints move on 6 % of the stop's ticks. n=6: 751 voxels a cloud, 67 % of the objects within 2 m and inside the babble's reach found, balls 21 %. Open a run's clouds afterwards with tools/run_voxel_viewer.sh LOG.jsonl (design doc §17.30, §17.31).

name: R52 · the gaze SWEEPS: at a stop the head never holds -- it moves at 0.3 rad/s toward the angle it has looked at least, and the cloud fills in
hint: WATCH (seed 3, fast-forward through 600 s; compare with R46 on the same seed -- the runs are identical until the first stop): the head keeps moving through every stop (97 % of ticks against 6 %), slowing to a quarter where the map finds the view new. n=6 against R46: voxels a cloud 751 -> 2271 on every seed, objects in reach found 67 -> 75 % (86 % when both arms stand the full 60 s), balls 21 -> 33 % (24 -> 40 %), the stack rule's precision 0.62 -> 0.92, stands 65/66 both. What to watch for: stops now run nearly the full 60 s (a moving view keeps the place map surprised: novel 18 -> 34 %, 5.7 more nodes), so it walks 7 m less. Part of the ball gain is the simulated one-ray-per-zone sensor. WORKING, not promoted (design doc §17.31).

name: R55 · the map reads the CLOUD, a stop ends when its cloud stops growing, and the head sweeps at a steady 0.6 rad/s (superseded by R56)
hint: SUPERSEDED by ★ CLOUD R56 (2026-09-15). PROMOTED (the operator's eye, 2026-09-15: "the best choice to promote -- faster head movement looks unnatural and does not seem to speed up stops"). WATCH (seed 5, fast-forward through 600 s): stops are short now (about 24 s against R52's 58) and end when the cloud stops filling in, not on a timer; the head sweeps at one steady speed through the whole stop; the duck walks twice as far between stops. n=6: map winner switches 77 -> 25 a minute, objects within 2 m in reach found 85 %, walls and furniture misread as small 2.3 %, stands 64/66. Watch the balls (23 %, the weakest number) and the walls on the longer walks. Compare R55b for the fastest head. PROMOTED (design doc §17.32).

name: R55b · as R55 with the head sweeping at 1.5 rad/s -- the fast end of the ladder
hint: WATCH (seed 5): the same short, cloud-ended stops as R55 with the head moving 2.5 times faster. n=6: objects in reach still found (87 %), balls 34 %, but walls start breaking into false small things (precision 0.71, 3.5 % misread) and stops are no shorter (24 s) -- speed does not buy tempo; the growth rule sets it. PARTIAL (design doc §17.32).

name: ★ CLOUD · R56 · the GLANCE: the head sweeps, the map reads the cloud, and a stop ends when the cloud stops growing (threshold 0.45, about 10 s)
hint: PROMOTED (the operator's eye, 2026-09-15: "the robot is able to make a very solid map in a very short amount of time"). WATCH (seed 3, fast-forward through 600 s): the R55 look with one change -- a stop ends once the cloud's growth falls below 45 % of its own peak (R55: 10 %). Stops of 7-15 s (median 10.5 s against R55's 20.7): the duck glances around and moves on. n=6 against R55: walls located 66 -> 70 % of the in-reach wall, objects within 2 m in reach found 85 -> 72 %, balls 23 -> 34 %, stands 66/66; the cost is walls and furniture read as small 2.3 -> 4.3 %. Compare R56b for the floor. PROMOTED (design doc §17.33).

name: R56b · as R56 at threshold 0.6 -- the shortest stops the rule allows (about 8 s)
hint: WATCH (seed 3): stops of 7-12 s, at the floor the 2 s judgement windows set. n=6: walls located 62 % and a quarter of clouds locate 29 % or less, the cloud 41 % thinner than R55's, precision 0.72, balls 23 %. PARTIAL (design doc §17.33).

name: R57 · THINGS: the stack rule runs in CloudMap, the nearest small cluster is attended, and a thing EPM earns a vocabulary over it (passive)
hint: PASSIVE: the ★ CLOUD walk is byte-identical (md5 guard); this adds the things reduction and its EPM and logs them. WATCH (seed 3, fast-forward through 600 s): nothing in the body changes yet -- read the cloud panel's things / small / attended counts at each stop. n=6: the module's clusters agree with the offline rule on 583/583; the attended thing is a real object on 73 % of ticks (misses: wall bases and chair legs seen as one column); the thing EPM's 35 nodes follow the sweep's fill-in state, not the object (purity 0.56, each object under 4+ winners). Compare R58: a two-column footprint floor and a shape-only descriptor. Things phase T1 (microduck_things_phase.md).

name: R58 · THINGS with a two-column footprint floor and a SHAPE-ONLY descriptor (sampling out of the vocabulary)
hint: MEASURED (n=6): two levers bundled, and they disagree. The two-column footprint floor raises attention precision 0.73 -> 0.82 (5+/1-: seeds 1,2,4,5,6 up, seed 3 0.56 -> 0.49) and keeps 82 % of the attended ticks (balls 96 %). The shape-only descriptor LOWERS the thing EPM's per-run purity 0.87 -> 0.83 (purity - chance +0.44 -> +0.30): hits per column is shape (a ball's curved face returns 8 per column, a block's flat face 18). Passive on every seed (md5). Superseded by R59 = the floor alone. Things phase T1 (microduck_things_phase.md; design doc §17.34).

name: R59 · THINGS with the two-column footprint floor alone (the full descriptor kept)
hint: MEASURED (n=6): the T1 config the seek loop builds on. Attention on a real object 0.73 -> 0.82 (5+/1-; seed 3 0.56 -> 0.49), the thing EPM's per-run purity 0.91 +- 0.07 (chance 0.52), 21 nodes a run, blocks and balls under separate nodes. Passive on every seed: the walk is byte-identical to ★ CLOUD, so there is nothing to see in the body yet -- read the cloud panel's things / small / attended at each stop (seed 3, fast-forward through 600 s). Things phase T1 WORKING (microduck_things_phase.md; design doc §17.34).

name: R60 · SEEK: a loop that walks to the attended thing, remembering where it was, and races play in the arbiter
hint: THE FIRST BEHAVIOURAL LEVER of the things phase (T2). WATCH (seed 3, fast-forward through 600 s): at the first stop the cloud attends a small thing; when the walk begins the duck heads for where it was (steer 3 in the log), and the arbiter hands the reference back to play once the range stops falling. On seed 3 the first target is a WALL BASE the rule read as small (the 18 % false-positive class), so the duck walks to the wall; seeds 5 and 6 walk onto blocks. n=6 vs R59: 21 episodes, 17 at a real object, blocks approached to 0.27 m median (7/11 within 0.4 m, 3 into contact), arrival by dead reckoning ends 20/21; walls 21.7 -> 12.4/min (4/6 seeds down), coverage and stands tie. WORKING as a mechanism, PARTIAL as a behaviour; not promoted. R60g adds --seek-gate (closer, but walls rise). Design doc §17.35.

name: R60g · SEEK with the sector gate: the target's ToF sector reads free while seek holds the reference (--seek-gate)
hint: MEASURED (n=6): closer approaches (blocks 11/14 within 0.4 m, balls 3/6, 5 episodes into contact) but walls 12.4 -> 28.9/min (up on 4/6 seeds; seed 4 to 80.9): a target by a wall, or a wall behind the thing, is what the sector gate hides. REGRESSION in this form; re-use: a gate limited to the last half metre, or opened only for a target whose vocabulary node is a thing's. Design doc §17.35.

name: R60a · SEEK + a stop that starts on ARRIVAL: the duck walks to a thing it saw and stops beside it (--stop-on-arrive)
hint: WATCH (seed 1, fast-forward through 600 s): from 772 s four arrival stops at a ball follow one another -- the duck reaches the ball at 0.2-0.3 m, stops, sweeps, sees it, walks the last step, stops again. n=6 (design doc §17.36): 32 arrival stops beginning a median 0.21 m from a real object (29/31 within 0.5 m); at 12/31 the stop's cloud attends nothing because the reached thing is below a level gaze (T3's case); walk 82 -> 54 %, coverage down, walls back to the base's level, a quarter of stops at the 60 s cap. WORKING as a mechanism, PARTIAL as a behaviour; not promoted. Next: the gaze at the reached thing (T3) and habituation.

name: R61 · SEEK + the heading REFLEX + play's target beyond the turning radius (R38's lookahead, retried now that the regulator regulates)
hint: (preset corrected 2026-09-17: it lacked --stop-on-arrive, which every measured arm had) MEASURED (n=6, with the heading reflex): REGRESSION -- the reference under play still moves at 0.60 rad/s and walls 64/min. Refuted on the mirrored bearing (O51); open again on R64. Design doc §17.37.

name: R62 · SEEK + the heading REFLEX + play's run-and-tumble WANDER on walks (a held random heading, 5 s runs)
hint: (preset corrected 2026-09-17: it lacked --stop-on-arrive, which every measured arm had) MEASURED (n=6, with the heading reflex): REGRESSION -- the reference under play moved at 1.5 rad/s, and its trace is what exposed the play loop's mirrored bearing (O51). Retry on R64. Design doc §17.37.

name: R63 · SEEK + the play loop in the duck's own handedness (heading_sign -1): its right is the body's right
hint: (preset corrected 2026-09-17: it lacked --stop-on-arrive, which every measured arm had) MEASURED (n=6): the premise holds -- with the sign right the reference under play stands still (0.00 rad/s, refFollow 0.11, the lowest measured); with the heading reflex the seek error closes to 0.26 rad and the yaw leaves its rail. Walls double (20 -> 47-49/min): the mirrored bearing had been an accidental avoider. Superseded by R64 (R48's step added). Design doc §17.37.

name: R64 · SEEK + play in the duck's handedness + R48's model-implied step (the loud avoider), with the heading reflex
hint: (preset corrected 2026-09-17: it lacked --stop-on-arrive, which every measured arm had) THE CANDIDATE for the operator's eye after the circling (2026-09-17). WATCH (seed 1, fast-forward through 600 s): the walks between stops go where the play or seek reference points, in wide arcs, instead of circling. n=6 vs R60a: the reference stands still under play (0.00 rad/s), coverage 89 -> 126 cells (5/6 up), path 81 -> 96 m, objects moved 2.5 -> 5.1 m, walls 20 -> 15/min with the spread gone (R60a 0-56, R64 3-24), straightness 0.15 -> 0.22, stands hold. The yaw command is still on its rail 93 % and the heading error still ~1 rad: the body follows in arcs. Compare R64r for the straight version. Design doc §17.37.

name: R64r · as R64 with the heading REFLEX (yaw closes the heading error in 1 s, released within 0.5 m of anything)
hint: (preset corrected 2026-09-17: it lacked --stop-on-arrive, which every measured arm had) WATCH (seed 1): the straight version -- while a loop holds the reference the yaw command closes the heading error (--heading-reflex 1.0 0.3 0.5). n=6: straightness 0.29 (R64 0.22), cells 144, the seek error 0.61 rad (R64 1.61), the yaw off its rail (69 % against 93 %); the cost is walls 15 -> 32/min and rescues 0.05 -> 0.19/min: a heading held to a reference AT a wall (a novel edge node, a wall base taken for a thing) beats the avoidance in the last half metre. WORKING on the channel, PARTIAL as a behaviour. Design doc §17.37.

name: R64w · the WALK the operator watched on 2026-09-17: R64 without arrival stops (timer stops only)
hint: The run the operator watched and liked on 2026-09-17 ('the directional fix is a big improvement; the robot is traversing much faster'); through a preset drift it had no --stop-on-arrive while the measured R64 did, so it is its own arm now. n=6 (design doc §17.38): walls 22/min (R64 with arrival stops 15), path 115 m, cells 140, straightness 0.28, walk 79 %, rescues 0.07/min. Seed 1: pushes a table leg ~880 s, falls over a block ~945 and ~1200 s. Timer stops every 80 s only.

name: R64s · the watched walk + a STUCK stop: a forward stall longer than 8x the body's own median stall starts a stop (--stop-on-stuck 8)
hint: MEASURED (n=6, design doc §17.38): 12 stuck stops over six runs, 8 at a wall or furniture; the long pushes 8 -> 5; walk 79 -> 71 %, path 115 -> 100 m, walls tie. WORKING as a mechanism, NULL as a behaviour: the duck stops, looks and resumes toward the same reference. WATCH (seed 1): the stop at the table leg ~880 s. Next: the stuck stop drops the seek target and bakes play's node.
